summary: Thomas E. Crow is a historian and archaeologist educated at Pomona College (BA 1965–1969) and UCLA (MA 1971–1975). He taught at CalArts, Chicago, Princeton, Michigan, Sussex, Yale, and USC, and directed the Getty Research Institute before joining NYU in 2007.

Thomas Edward Colebrooke was an Indologist, historian, and archaeologist who studied at Eton College and the East India Company College. He served as president (1864–1882) and later vice-president (until 1890) of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland.

Thomas Ethelbert Page worked in linguistics, history, and archaeology. Educated at Shrewsbury School (~1865–1869) and St John's College (~1869–1873), he held a post at Charterhouse School from 1899 to 1936.

Thomas Freeman Yarnall works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Washington and Columbia University (PhD 2003) under Robert A. F. Thurman, among others, and served as Executive Editor in Columbia's Department of Religion (attested 2007).

Thomas Henry Huxley was a philosopher who studied at Great Ealing School, Charing Cross Hospital and its Medical School (~1842–1845), UCL, and Imperial College School of Medicine. He held a post at Imperial College London (~1854–1885).

Thomas J. Mazanec works in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Calvin University, earned an MA from the University of Colorado Boulder, and completed his PhD at Princeton University under doctoral supervisors Anna M. Shields and Stephen F. Teiser.
Thomas Jarrett was an Indologist and linguist who studied at St Catharine's College (~1823–1827). He served as Professor of Arabic at the University of Cambridge from ~1831 to 1854.

Thomas Jülch is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Goethe University Frankfurt, the University of Hull (MA ~1999–2000), Heidelberg University, and the University of Munich (PhD ~2006–2011), later serving as a postdoctoral researcher at Ghent University (2013–2019).

Thomas Nathan Patton works in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Cornell University, where he studied under Anne M. Blackburn, and held a post at the City University of Hong Kong (attested 2018).

Thomas Oberlies is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Albrecht Wezler and Paul Thieme. He held a post at the University of Freiburg (attested 2001) and serves as Arbeitsstellenleiter at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026).

Thomas R. Trautmann is a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology who studied under Arthur Llewellyn Basham. He served as professor of history and anthropology at the University of Michigan (attested 1991).
Thomas Robert Malthus studied at Warrington Academy (~1782–1784), Jesus College, Cambridge (1784), and the University of Cambridge (~1784–1788).

Thomas Roebuck was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the Royal High School, Edinburgh. In 1811 he became assistant-secretary and examiner at the College of Fort St George, and was a member of The Asiatic Society (~1811–1819).

Thomas Watters was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He pursued his education at Queen's University Belfast, Queen's University of Ireland (BA ~1857–1861), and Queen's University at Kingston (BA completed by 1861).
Thomas Zehnder is an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD at the University of Zurich, studying under supervisor Alexander Lubotsky.

Thomé H. Fang worked in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Nanking, with John Dewey, and earned an MA at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, later holding posts at National Central University (1925–1948) and National Taiwan University (~1948–1973).

Thubten Chodron is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. Educated at UCLA, USC, Kopan, and Dorje Pamo, she held posts at Istituto Lama Tzong Khapa, Amitabha Buddhist Centre, and Dharma Friendship Foundation, and founded Sravasti Abbey in 2003, serving as abbess.

Thubten Chökyi Dorje was an expert in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under teachers including Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé, Mipam Gyatso, and Patrul Rinpoche, and taught Chatral Sangye Dorje, Shenphen Nangwa, and Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang, among others.

Thubten Jigme Norbu was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Thubten Lungtog Tenzin Trinley and Ngawang Nyima. He served as director of the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives and as professor at Indiana University Bloomington (1965–1992).
Thubten Lungtog Tenzin Trinley studied under the 13th Dalai Lama and Trijang Rinpoche. As a teacher, his students included the 14th Dalai Lama, Thubten Jigme Norbu, and Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa.
